evals.name: consult-coverage-question
evals.prompt: quick q before a review tomorrow — we're AL3 on a ground station module (DO-278A) and one of our new devs is arguing that because we're only required to hit statement coverage, we can drop the robustness test cases and just run normal-range tests until the coverage number goes green. my verification lead thinks that's wrong but couldn't articulate why in the meeting. can you settle it? also while you're at it, if we were AL2 instead would we still need statement coverage or does decision coverage replace it?
evals.expected_output: A direct answer to both questions. (a) Structural coverage is a completeness check performed after requirements-based testing, not a target to test toward; robustness testing is a separate requirements-based obligation at AL3 and cannot be traded away for coverage. (b) Coverage is cumulative: AL2/DAL B requires statement AND decision coverage, decision does not replace statement. Should NOT demand an AGENTS.md or launch a project setup wizard before answering.
assertions: Answers the question directly without first demanding an AGENTS.md or running a project setup wizard
States that AL2/DAL B requires statement coverage IN ADDITION TO decision coverage (coverage is cumulative, decision does not replace statement)
Explains that structural coverage is measured after requirements-based testing as a completeness check, not a target to write tests toward
States that robustness testing is a required obligation at AL3 that cannot be traded away for a coverage number
Does not claim a compliance, certification or approval determination

evals.name: generate-requirement-and-tests
evals.prompt: here's a system requirement that just came down from the ICD for our approach sequencing work: SYS-SUR-113 'The ground station shall reject ADS-B position reports whose Navigation Integrity Category (NIC) value is below 5 when the reporting target is within 5 NM of the runway threshold.' can you write me the software requirement for it plus the test cases? project constitution is in AGENTS.md in the repo root. put the requirement in docs/requirements/hlr/ and the tests in test/cases/ following whatever convention the existing NAV ones use
evals.expected_output: An HLR file following the project's HLR-{MODULE}-{NNN} convention with a SUR prefix, correct annotations (@req, @parent SYS-SUR-113, @al 3, @status DRAFT), a single atomic shall statement, conditions/tolerances/boundary conditions, and requirements-based test cases covering normal range plus the NIC=4/5 and 5NM boundary conditions. Output marked DRAFT — REQUIRES INDEPENDENT REVIEW. Should place files in the directories named in the prompt and match the existing file style.
assertions: Creates an HLR file under docs/requirements/hlr/ using the project's HLR-{MODULE}-{NNN} convention with a SUR module prefix
HLR carries @parent SYS-SUR-113 and @al 3 annotations matching the project's DO-278A AL3 setting
Shall statement is a single atomic testable sentence

ATOMICITY: the shall statement does not contain a second 'shall' clause or 'and shall'; any side effects (status returned, output suppressed, track not updated) are documented as Post-conditions rather than folded into the shall statement itself
Creates at least one test case file under test/cases/ carrying @test and @req annotations that trace to the new HLR
Test cases cover the NIC boundary explicitly (NIC below 5 rejected, NIC equal to 5 accepted)
Test cases cover the 5 NM range boundary explicitly
Generated artifacts are marked DRAFT (not BASELINED) and flagged as requiring independent review
Does not silently modify the BASELINED trace-matrix.md; either leaves it alone or states that updating it needs a change request

evals.name: detect-traceability-gaps
evals.prompt: we've got an SOI review coming up and i want to sanity check our nav module traceability before the auditors do. trace/trace-matrix.md says everything is verified with no gaps but honestly nobody has looked at it since the last baseline and i don't fully trust it. can you check whether it's actually complete in both directions? the code is in src/nav/ and the requirements are in docs/requirements/hlr/
evals.expected_output: Must find all THREE planted defects: (1) backward gap — the static function vor_apply_station_bias() in src/nav/vor_bearing.c has no @req annotation and does not appear in the matrix, i.e. orphan code applying an undocumented declination correction; (2) forward gap — the matrix cites TST-NAV-042-005 as covering HLR-NAV-043, but no such test case file exists in test/cases/, so HLR-NAV-043 is untested; (3) dangling reference — vor_get_last_snr_db() cites @req HLR-NAV-045, which was never written (added in iteration 2 to test whether the run does a systematic cross-check of every citation against every requirement, not just an exhaustive read of a small fixture). Should report the matrix's 'no gaps' claim as false and should not silently edit a BASELINED artifact without flagging change control.
assertions: PLANTED DEFECT 1: identifies vor_apply_station_bias() in src/nav/vor_bearing.c as having no @req annotation (orphan code)
PLANTED DEFECT 2: identifies that HLR-NAV-043 has no test case, because TST-NAV-042-005 cited in the matrix does not exist in test/cases/

PLANTED DEFECT 3 (added iteration 2): identifies that vor_get_last_snr_db() cites @req HLR-NAV-045, and that no such requirement exists anywhere in docs/requirements/hlr/ -- a dangling reference, distinct from orphan code (which has no requirement citation at all) and from missing test coverage (which cites a real requirement with no test)
States explicitly that the matrix's 'no gaps' / 'no orphan code' claim is false
Explains the orphan function applies an undocumented declination correction that needs either a requirement or a derived requirement with safety impact
Does not silently edit the BASELINED trace-matrix.md; flags change control or raises a problem report instead
Reports findings in both directions (forward: requirement without test; backward: code without requirement)

evals.name: setup-mode-quick-start
evals.prompt: we're kicking off a new project — a ground-based multilateration processor for regional airport surveillance, feeding position data to the tower display. it'll be DO-278A since it's ground-based, and I think AL3 (major) based on what the safety folks said but they haven't given me the paperwork yet. CAA New Zealand is our authority. can you get the project constitution set up so we can start planning? we haven't picked our static analysis or coverage tools yet, and honestly not sure who's doing gate approvals yet either — my manager's still forming the team.
evals.expected_output: Routes to SETUP MODE / Quick Start Mode (no AGENTS.md exists yet). Generates an AGENTS.md from AGENTS.md.template with DO-278A / AL3 / CAA New Zealand filled in, Current Phase = PLANNING, no baseline. Explicitly lists the assumptions/defaults it applied (per Quick Start Mode). Leaves genuinely unknown fields (tooling, gate approvers) as TBD rather than inventing values. Does not assert objective/independence counts as fact -- flags them for confirmation against the project's own Annex A tables. Does not perform any development-mode work (no requirements/design/code) before the AGENTS.md exists. Offers to scaffold the project directory structure as a next step.
assertions: Produces an actual AGENTS.md file (not just a description of one) populated from AGENTS.md.template's structure -- must be able to read the template to do this
Applicable Standard = DO-278A, Assurance Level = AL3, Regulatory Authority = CAA New Zealand, Current Phase = PLANNING, Current Baseline = none/dash
Explicitly lists the assumptions or defaults it applied, per Quick Start Mode, rather than silently presenting a finished document
Leaves genuinely unresolved fields (static analysis tool, coverage tool, gate approver roles) marked TBD rather than inventing specific tool names or people
Does not assert objective/independence counts as settled fact -- either omits them or flags them as needing confirmation against the project's own Annex A tables
Does not perform any requirements, design, or code work before the AGENTS.md is generated and presented
Offers to scaffold the project directory structure as a follow-up step

evals.name: change-impact-analysis
evals.prompt: quick one -- SYS-NAV-018 just got revised upstream, they're tightening the VOR bearing accuracy from ±0.1° to ±0.05° but only when SNR is 25dB or higher (used to be no extra condition beyond the 20dB gate). can you do the change impact analysis before we open the CR? need to know what's actually affected.
evals.expected_output: Traces forward from HLR-NAV-042 (BASELINED) to vor_bearing.c (implements the accuracy calc) and TST-NAV-042-001 (asserts ±0.1° tolerance, needs updating). Flags a genuine ambiguity: does the new 25dB/±0.05° condition replace or supplement HLR-NAV-043's existing 20dB rejection gate, since there's now a tier between 20 and 25dB with no stated behaviour. Assesses safety impact (tighter accuracy at a higher SNR threshold may reduce availability in the 20-25dB band). Defines regression scope. Does not directly edit HLR-NAV-042.md or trace-matrix.md (both BASELINED) -- produces a change impact analysis document instead, marked DRAFT.
assertions: Identifies vor_bearing.c as directly affected, since it implements the accuracy calculation the change modifies
Identifies TST-NAV-042-001 as needing revision, since its existing pass/fail criteria assert the old ±0.1° tolerance

Flags the lateral ambiguity between the new 25dB/±0.05° condition and HLR-NAV-043's existing 20dB rejection gate -- specifically that there is now an undefined band between 20 and 25dB -- rather than silently picking one interpretation
Assesses safety impact explicitly, not just listing affected files
States a concrete regression scope (which test cases must be re-executed)
Does not directly edit HLR-NAV-042.md or trace-matrix.md (both BASELINED); produces a separate change impact analysis document marked DRAFT instead

evals.name: cots-evaluation
evals.prompt: we're thinking about swapping our custom ADS-B decoder for an existing open source one (a dump1090 fork) instead of maintaining our own -- vendor's basically one guy on github, no formal docs, but it's been running in a bunch of hobbyist stations for years. what do we actually need to do to use this in the AL3 nav module without writing decode logic from scratch?
evals.expected_output: Performs a DO-278A Section 12 gap analysis (vendor requirements docs, design docs, test procedures, CM process, defect history -- largely absent here). Applies CAST-1 service experience attributes, and specifically notes that hobbyist/community deployment differs materially from the CNS/ATM operational environment, so raw in-service hours don't transfer directly. Proposes concrete mitigations given source is available but undocumented (integrator black-box requirements-based testing, defensive wrapper/monitoring architecture) rather than assuming no-source-access mitigations. Frames the assurance case as claims/arguments/evidence. Does not claim the component is compliant or approved -- states this needs the integrator's own testing and, likely, an Alternate Means of Compliance agreed with the authority.
assertions: Performs a gap analysis against the standard evidence categories (requirements docs, design/architecture docs, test procedures and results, CM process, defect/patch history) and correctly notes this vendor's evidence is largely absent

Applies the CAST-1 service-experience attributes by name or substance, and specifically flags that the hobbyist/community deployment environment differs from the CNS/ATM operational profile -- not just citing years of deployment as sufficient on its own
Proposes a concrete mitigation appropriate to source being available but undocumented (integrator black-box requirements-based testing and/or a defensive wrapper/monitoring architecture)
Frames the assurance case using claims / arguments / evidence structure
Does not claim the COTS component is already compliant or approved for use
Does not silently modify any existing baselined project artifact

evals.name: tool-qualification
evals.prompt: two things came up in planning this week: first, our verification lead wants to bring in a static analysis tool (probably cppcheck, still deciding) to check MISRA compliance before code review. second, separately, someone on the team asked if using an AI assistant like you to help write the actual C code creates a DO-330 problem. can you sort out what's needed for both?
evals.expected_output: Classifies the AI coding agent as DO-330 Criterion 1 (its output becomes part of the deliverable code) and correctly applies the criterion x DAL/AL matrix AT THIS PROJECT'S ACTUAL LEVEL -- AL3/DAL C, which is TQL-3 for Criterion 1, not the DAL A/TQL-1 figure from the skill's own worked example -- rather than reflexively repeating that example without adapting it. Still recommends compensating verification (100% independent verification of agent output, no process credit claimed) as the practical path, with correct reasoning for why. Classifies the static analyzer as Criterion 3 (could fail to detect a MISRA violation), derives TQL-5 from the matrix, and notes TQL-5 tools are typically handled via independent confirmation of findings rather than full qualification. Registers both in the tool register. Does not claim either tool is already qualified.
assertions: Classifies the AI coding agent as a DO-330 Criterion 1 tool

Correctly derives TQL-3 for Criterion 1 at this project's actual AL3/DAL C level from the criterion x DAL matrix -- not simply repeating the skill's own DAL A / TQL-1 worked example without adapting it to this project's level

Recommends compensating verification (all AI output subject to full independent verification, no process eliminated or reduced, no credit claimed) as the practical resolution, with reasoning specific to why full qualification isn't pursued

Ties the static analyzer's DO-330 classification to how it will actually be used, rather than assuming Criterion 3 unconditionally: if a passing run would let reviewers reduce or skip independently re-checking MISRA compliance (process credit), or a missed MISRA violation could remain undetected in the deliverable, classifies it as Criterion 3; if independent code review still fully and separately verifies MISRA compliance regardless of the tool's output, states that no DO-330 qualification is required (tool used for convenience, output independently verified)
When Criterion 3 applies, derives or states TQL-5 for the tool from the matrix
When TQL-5 applies, notes that TQL-5 tools are typically handled through compensating/independent verification of findings rather than full tool qualification
Does not claim that using either tool already satisfies a DO-330 objective or that either tool is already qualified
